subject.title: Bug: sandbox.mode: "non-main" silently breaks sessions_spawn subagent initialization

question: For defaults-level `non-main` sandboxed `sessions_spawn` failures, should OpenClaw keep the accepted async spawn contract and terminalize/log startup failure, or preflight sandbox startup before returning accepted?
rationale: Both approaches can fix the user-visible hang, but the choice affects gateway acceptance semantics, `agent.wait`, subagent registry state, session projections, and the overlapping startup-lifecycle work.

options.title: Terminalize Async Startup Failure
options.body: Keep the accepted spawn contract, but emit/log a typed startup failure and prove registry, history, list, and wait callers see it for Docker sandbox startup failures.

options.title: Preflight Before Accept
options.body: Move enough sandbox startup validation before the accepted response to reject immediately, accepting extra latency and compatibility impact for existing callers.

options.title: Defer To Lifecycle Contract
options.body: Keep this issue open as the sandbox-specific proof case while maintainers decide the broader startup lifecycle direction in the related issue and PR.

recommendation.title: Terminalize Async Startup Failure
recommendation.body: Keep the accepted spawn contract, but emit/log a typed startup failure and prove registry, history, list, and wait callers see it for Docker sandbox startup failures.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal spans subagent lifecycle, registry, sandbox inheritance, and gateway/session behavior affected by the contract choice.
